note.surface: ROOT CAUSE + FIX: vLLM custom-allreduce cross-rank memory-ordering race on gfx908. The 1stage/2stage reduce kernels synchronized peer-data visibility with a fully-RELAXED barrier_at_start + DEVICE-scope flag acquires; device-scope acquire does not cover remote agents' writes on gfx908, so a consumer kernel could read a peer-staged residual value before it landed — a torn bf16 read produces arbitrary bit patterns: NaN seeds (NaN flavor) or huge-finite values (flat flavor) in ONE layer's forward, committing a junk token whose spam wall then self-sustains (SW window fill + draft-codebook exclusion) with acceptance=1.0 forever. The fork had itself documented the adjacent hazard ('HIP IPC views of cached memory don't see peer writes -> drift -> NaN') and relied on uncached-allocation side effects.

evidence.forensics: 7 captures: every kill = one-layer corruption between clean neighbors; int8 act-quant LAUNDERS NaN (qkvz 'clean' while bf16 ba projection exposed it); the residual-write/read seam was pinpointed by perturbation-masking (any extra kernel in the seam suppresses the kill — 3 clean boots); static audit (subagent) eliminated all host-side ordering and identified the in-kernel visibility seams

note.fix: csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh + csrc/custom_collective_common.cuh: reduce kernels now call barrier_at_start_release (RELEASE store + ACQUIRE wait — the correct variant existed unused in-tree); all cross-rank flag acquires promoted to SYSTEM scope. Rebuilt _C_stable_libtorch.
